 Health officials issue a mosquito-borne illness advisory and urge residents to protect themselves from bites
 By Brody Wooddell, WFTV.com October 21, 2026 at 10:35 am EDT Enter Fullscreen Expand Orange County to spray for mosquitoes after 5 dengue fever cases Health officials issued a mosquito-borne illness advisory Wednesday after confirming a human case of locally acquired dengue in Seminole County.
The Florida Department of Health in Seminole County and Seminole County Mosquito Control are coordinating surveillance, prevention and control efforts, according to the announcement. By Brody Wooddell, WFTV.com October 21, 2026 at 10:35 am EDT SEMINOLE COUNTY, Fla. — Health officials issued a mosquito-borne illness advisory Wednesday after confirming a human case of locally acquired dengue in Seminole County.
 The Florida Department of Health in Seminole County and Seminole County Mosquito Control are coordinating surveillance, prevention and control efforts, according to the announcement.
 Officials did not release the patient’s condition, the location within the county or when the infection was identified.
 Residents urged to prevent mosquito bites
 The health department urged residents to take precautions against mosquito bites and shared a mosquito prevention guide .
 The department continues to monitor mosquito-borne illnesses statewide, including dengue, West Nile virus, Eastern equine encephalitis, St. Louis encephalitis, malaria and chikungunya.
 Residents can find additional information on the Florida Department of Health’s mosquito prevention webpage or call DOH-Seminole at 407-665-3243.
